title: Evaluate Undo granularity during post-reset removal of non-recurring items
scope: Per-action Undo implementation and automated verification completed under the user's 2026-11-07 unattended authorization. User tested and accepted the per-action policy and fix on 2026-11-07.
user_report: The primary deletion use case is removing non-recurring items after Reset checks. If several intentional removals are followed by one mistake, Undo returns all removed items, forcing the user to repeat the intentional cleanup. The user suggests a Gmail-like single-item stack and asks for alternatives; exact current Gmail behavior has not been verified or adopted as a requirement.

evidence.user_observation: User reports the restore-all outcome during real use; device/build and precise action sequence were not specified.
evidence.source_review: UndoRemove::mergeWith appends consecutive commands' removed items and updateText reports their total count. UndoRemove::undo restores every member of the merged command. Model already owns QUndoStack. UI-023 explicitly records the previous user-selected policy: restore the whole deletion batch, each deletion restarting 15 seconds.
evidence.validation_gap: No new workflow reproduction, automated test or phone study was run for this intake. Existing batch restoration tests establish the current policy, not its usability for post-reset cleanup.

primary_scenario: Use disposable mixed recurring/non-recurring items, complete a shopping trip, and Reset checks. Establish the resulting order before cleanup, preserving UI-009 semantics.
Deliberately delete Birthday candles, then Gift wrap, as two separate swipes within the recovery window.
Accidentally delete Milk and activate Undo with one hand.

Record exactly which items return, their identities/order/check flags, message clarity, time and additional gestures needed to finish cleanup. Current batching restores all three; the proposed behavior restores only Milk.

proposal.granularity: One Undo step per user deletion action. A single swipe is one item; an explicit Remove checked or Clear list action is one coherent bulk operation. Do not automatically merge separate swipes into one restore-all action.
proposal.interaction: Keep the existing whole-bar Undo and animated countdown. Identify the latest action/item. A tap restores only that action; deliberate further taps can undo earlier pending actions in reverse order. No additional Undo-all button or history screen is proposed.
proposal.simplicity: Evaluate reusing the existing QUndoStack and UUID/neighbor restoration. Prefer one shared bounded recovery clock rather than separate timers for every item. Recovery expiry/pause/restart behavior must be decided explicitly before implementation.
proposal.alternative: Latest-action-only Undo would be simpler to explain but makes earlier accidental deletions unrecoverable as soon as a newer deletion replaces them. Compare that tradeoff against a short per-action stack rather than adopting it silently.
proposal.acceptance: Recommendation only; final interaction and timer policy remain undecided.

review_and_test_cases: Real one-handed Android cleanup after Reset, including an accidental removal in the middle or at the end of several intended removals and a mistake noticed after another deletion.
Repeated Undo taps, accidental double taps, clear identification of the next action, deletion after Undo, and expiry while earlier actions remain pending.
A single bulk Remove checked/Clear list action, separate bulk actions, and a bulk action adjacent to individual swipes. Define which operation one Undo reverses.
Preserve the post-reset order, surviving/newly entered items, original UUIDs and check flags, pending editor drafts, scrolling and reorder behavior.
Retain reachable placement above native IME/safe areas, drawer/background pause policy, and deliberate list-switch/reload boundaries. Cross-restart recovery is not newly requested.

If a policy change is selected, add automated model/UI regression assertions first against the actual reset/delete/mistake/Undo sequence; prove the current implementation fails the newly accepted expectation and the change passes. Supplement with actual Android touch/IME verification and record limits.
acceptance_criteria: Document current outcomes separately from the usability concern and possible replacement policies.
Evaluate post-reset cleanup on a physical phone with disposable data and propose the simplest policy that corrects one mistake without reversing intended cleanup.
Agree on individual/bulk granularity, repeated Undo behavior, message and recovery-window rules before implementation.
If selected for implementation, update DESIGN.md and affected batch assertions intentionally, retain permanent failing-before/passing-after coverage, and record phone confirmation before closure.

selected_policy.granularity: One step per swipe; one step for each explicit bulk Remove checked/Clear list. No merging across user actions.
selected_policy.interaction: Existing whole-bar tap restores the latest action. Further taps restore earlier pending actions. Message identifies the next action. No Undo-all/history screen.
selected_policy.clock: One shared 15-second recovery window. Each deletion restarts it; Undo does not extend it. Expiry discards all remaining steps. Drawer/app-inactive pause behavior is retained.
selected_policy.boundaries: Keep existing current-list/process/reload boundaries, identity/neighbor restoration and preservation of newer edits. New deletion after Undo discards undone future actions through QUndoStack.

implementation: Remove UndoRemove id()/mergeWith() overrides so the existing QUndoStack keeps commands separate. Bulk operations already construct one command containing their removed records. No new history engine, UI component, timer or message strings.

Initial driver used a numeric-item flag predicate; that fixture-only assertion was corrected before retaining actual failing Undo evidence.
regression.model_after: out/ux005/model-all.txt: all 104 model records pass, including new policy and existing mutations, pending edits, identity, read-only and persistence cases.
regression.remaining: No remaining implementation or regression gap within the user-accepted scope; specific dictation/accessibility studies were not claimed by this acceptance.
regression.android_cleanup_after: out/ux005/android-cleanup: all six checks pass. Real checks, Reset, three cleanup swipes, one-action-per-tap Undo and restart preserve exact UUIDs/order/flags. The real-keyboard/recovery matrix also passes all 24 checks in both themes.
regression.android_recovery_after: out/ux005/android-recovery-final: all 24 native checks pass in Light/Dark. Separate Undo steps preserve a newly submitted item and original identities/order, retain Gboard, expire after the actual timeout, and pause/resume in background. An intermediate driver requested an idle UiAutomator dump during the animated countdown; that invalid probe was removed in favor of the existing rendered-bar approach. Two-pending-step expiry remains covered by the permanent QML test.

resolution.summary: One Undo step per deletion action, coherent bulk operations and repeated recovery through the existing QUndoStack; retain the shared 15-second clock.
